text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- AMID CPMF TAX CONCERNS, SAVINGS ACCOUNTS BEAT RECORD

Savings in December reached their highest level since the Real anti-inflation plan was introduced in mid-1994, the Central Bank said. The reason: consumers are increasingly wary of the new 0.2 percent CPMF "check tax" on all financial transactions.
-- PAPER FIRM SUZANO SECURITIZES $100 MILLION IN EXPORTS
Pulp and paper firm Cia Suzano de Papel e Celulose ended 1996 by securitizing some $100 million in exports, selling debt to five U.S. insurers.
-- COMMERCIAL FIRMS BEGIN NEW YEAR WITH STOCKS

Brazilian commercial firms began the year with stocks, the result of a slowdown in economic activity. The Sao Paulo Commercial Association released December figures showing the month was worse than is normal for the Christmas season.
O GLOBO
-- RIO MAYOR TO EXPAND TUNNEL ENTRANCES
Luiz Paulo Conde, Rio de Janeiro's new mayor, said he plans to complete projects begun by his predecessor as well as lengthen and expand the accesses to several city tunnels.
-- SURGERY SIDELINES FORMER SAO PAULO MAYOR FOR 30 DAYS

Former Sao Paulo mayor Paulo Maluf underwent prostate surgery that is likely to sideline the presidential hopeful for 30 days, during which Brazilian lawmakers are expected to vote on President Fernando Henrique's re-election bill. Maluf opposes the measure.
-- CENTRAL BANK UNVEILS CPMF TAX RULES
The Central Bank yesterday unveiled rules for levying the new CPMF "check tax" on financial transactions, which is expected to go into effect January 25.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- BRAZIL RECEIVES RECORD INVESTMENT IN 1996
Direct foreign investment entering Brazil reached a record $9 billion in 1996, up a whopping 174 percent from 1995 when $3.285 billion entered the country.
-- MALUF UNDERGOES PROSTATE SURGERY

Former Sao Paulo mayor Paulo Maluf, 65, underwent surgery to remove his prostate and is expected to be released from the hospital in four days while tests are conducted to determine if a tumor detected in the gland is malignant.
-- NUMBER OF VACCINATED CHILDREN FALLS IN 1996
The number of one-year-old babies vaccinated against polio, measles, tetanus, whooping cough and diphteria fell in 1996 compared with the prior year, the Health Ministry said.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
